title: Suzanne Wright stays in apartment until death
what_changed: Suzanne was able to remain in her Bethesda Gardens apartment with her belongings until she passed away, avoiding a move during declining health.
span_text: After her mother's health started declining in March 2012, Janet said the ability for her mother to remain in her apartment made a big difference in the quality of life in her final days. Suzanne passed on Feb. 20, 2013. 'We were able to keep her where she had made a lot of friends so that, when she was able to be social, she was surrounded by people, she could get to the dining room or have visitors there,' Janet said. 'Moving her at that point in her health and age would not have been ideal.' Her mother was able to remain in her beloved Bethesda Gardens apartment thanks to Bethesda's Geriatric Care Management program, a service offered through Bethesda Senior Support Solutions that benefits residents and members of the community by providing free counseling and coordination of care. title: Breadwinner eliminates arrears and starts business
primary_beneficiary: the sole breadwinner in his household
what_changed: ERAP eliminated his rental arrears, helped them stay housed, and with another program he established his own successful business and is in a more financially sustainable position.
span_text: The sole breadwinner in his household lost his job as a janitor during the pandemic. He struggled to keep up with rent payments and provide for his family, including his wife who is disabled and sister who is ill. When he received an eviction notice he took out a high-interest loan to help maintain their housing. ERAP provided support to eliminate his rental arrears and help them stay housed. With support from another program, he was able to invest in cleaning equipment, establish his own successful business, and is in a more financially sustainable position today.

title: Three resident success stories
primary_beneficiary: a young mother, a senior citizen, a young father
what_changed: The young mother earned a health care certification and works a living-wage job; the senior received a Thanksgiving food basket; the father caught up on bills and bought school supplies.
span_text: At River Garden, a young mother enrolled in Clover Career Connections' job training program, earned her health care certification and is now working a living wage full-time job with benefits. At Columbia Parc, a senior citizen received a Thanksgiving food basket through a coordinated opportunity with New Orleans Saints player Johnathan Abrams, and was grateful for the dignity and connection it provided. Through Clover's free VITA tax preparation service, a young father received his earned income tax credit and refund, which gave him the power to catch up on bills and purchase school supplies for his children, right when it mattered most.

title: Free shares to refugee families
what_changed: 60 refugee families received free fresh produce shares.
span_text: In 2021 we supplied fresh, nutritionally-dense produce to 630 members over the span of 40 weeks.  We strongly believe that everyone should have access to nutritionally dense, local food, especially those who experience poverty and food insecurity. That's why in 2021 we offered: 60 free shares to refugee families in partnership with the Refugee Development Center, 38 subsidized shares for folks who were experiencing hardship, and 16 shares for folks who wanted to pay using SNAP benefits.

title: Graduate finds joy and hope through obedience
what_changed: He now feels joyful and hopeful about his future instead of unsure and insecure.
span_text: Our interviewees repeated back to us many of the lessons they learned and explained how those foundational truths are still relevant to their daily lives. 'In God's economy, success isn't measured by results…it's measured by obedience,' one responded. He went on to share how he tries every day to walk in obedience to God while trusting God with all the outcomes in his life. This results in his feeling joyful and hopeful about his future whereas before NG, he was unsure and insecure. 'Know the truth, believe the truth, take action on the truth and your feelings will get in line…sometimes' was another truth that a young man shared. He explained how knowing the truth of his identity in Christ informs how he should act daily, even when he doesn't feel like it. Over time, he knows that if he will be faithful to ACT on the truth, his feelings will begin to line up with his actions instead of t

title: Worker engagement reduces emissions
what_changed: Created a culture of sustainability on the farms and reduced CO2 emissions by the equivalent of 1 million miles driven.
span_text: EFI partnered with Measure to Improve and three California-based farming operations to pilot a program to demonstrate how worker engagement in the design of waste management practices could help reduce agricultural greenhouse gas emissions. The program was successful in creating a culture of sustainability on the farms and reducing CO2 emissions during the pilot by the equivalent of 1 million miles driven by an average gasoline-powered vehicle.

title: Widowed mother gains housing stability
primary_beneficiary: Marita, a single parent of three young children
what_changed: ERAP covered her rental arrears and provided her family with housing stability through a challenging time.
span_text: After losing her husband to COVID, Marita took on parenting their three young children as a single parent. When her car broke down, she used her minimal savings to purchase a used car to maintain her employment. With her savings depleted, she found herself unable to cover monthly expenses. She fell behind on rent and received a letter of eviction. ERAP covered her rental arrears and provided her family with housing stability through a challenging time.

title: Graduate's transformation from suicide attempt
what_changed: He went from suicidal depression and self-loathing to a transformed life with a personal relationship with Christ, a fulfilling career, marriage, and fatherhood.
span_text: I t culminated with a suicide attempt. I believed Christianity was a legalistic set of rules you had to live your life by, and I perceived God as a very distant, judgmental authority figure. All of this led to crippling depression. I was depressed for years and years. It got to the point I was planning to take my life and had a couple of thwarted attempts. Then somebody mentioned Narrow Gate to me. I was resistant to Narrow Gate at first, to be honest. It sounded terrible on paper: 'Let's give up your phone and independence and go live in the woods for eight months.' But I was desperate. I didn't know 'who' I was, or 'why' I was. I sometimes will think back to things that happened before Narrow Gate and it feels like they're someone else's memories because I'm so radically changed by coming to have an actual, personal relationship with Christ - a thing I didn't know existed prior to that

title: Resistant resident calmed by volunteer
primary_beneficiary: a new resident who resisted medications
what_changed: The resident became calm, opened her eyes, and felt the volunteer knew exactly what she needed to hear.
span_text: ' A s a volunteer at Celia's House, I have had many moving experiences, but one that immediately comes to mind is about a new resident who resisted taking medications. She was a former nurse and wanted to be aware during her dying experience. I entered her room and began quietly reading from a little book of wisdom. I sang between the short readings and stroked her head gently. After some time, the resident became calm, opened her eyes wide, looked at me, and asked, 'How could you, a perfect stranger, know exactly what I needed to hear at this exact time?' I looked at her thoughtfully and asked myself the same question. I felt honored to have been one of her last encounters on this side.' -Janet, spiritual care volunteer and retired professional singer

title: Robert's release and new career
primary_beneficiary: Robert (incarcerated man sentenced to 44 years to life)
what_changed: Robert was resentenced and released in December 2023, found a job as a Program Coordinator for a recovery service program, and is now a productive, law-abiding member of society.
span_text: 'Robert' was sentenced to 44 years - life in prison after being convicted of 2nd degree murder, assaulting a police officer, and fleeing after shooting and killing the man who disrespected his then wife. With no end in sight and while serving his time in custody, 'Robert' enrolled in and completed Integrated Substance Use Disorder Treatment Program (ISUDT). Shortly afterwards, he went on to successfully completing the Offender Mentor Certification Program. He was then assigned to Phoenix House' ISUDT Program at Ironwood State Prison in Blythe as an OMCP Mentor. His exemplary efforts in performing all his duties and responsibilities transformed him into a model mentor, helping others change their mindset and set positive goals for their future. As a result of 'Robert's' efforts and exceptional performance in these programs and good behavior, he was resentenced and released in December 202

title: Kade graduates on time with diploma

Once we were able to help Kade's family stabilize, he flourished. He worked diligently to recover his credits and was able to graduate on time with his diploma. During his stay, Greg learned to replace his aggressive responses with words, learning to share his feelings verbally instead of physically. title: Energy retrofits on 30 homes
what_changed: Over 80 free energy assessments were conducted and retrofits were started or completed on 30 homes, making homes more energy efficient and affordable.
span_text: Last year, CAN made significant strides in promoting sustainability and energy efficiency in the Bryant neighborhood. With the help of key partnerships  and  funding  from  MSHDA,  Builders Initiative, and the McKnight Foundation, we conducted  over  80  free  energy  assessments  and started  or  completed  retrofits  on  30  homes.  Our primary partner, the City of Ann Arbor, received a Department of Energy planning grant to explore the feasibility of a regional geothermal district, with the Bryant neighborhood as a central focus. Community engagement remains a key priority as we work to bring more residents into this transformative initiative. Thanks to our collaborative efforts,  funding  is  secured  to  upgrade  about  70 homes,  making  homes  more  energy  efficient  and affordable for residents.

span_text: Due to multiple health struggles, Ms. C has found herself regularly in a wheelchair. This has made getting in and out of her house difficult because of four steps at the front door and a narrow rear door. Ms. C went through the eligibility and home assessment process with Healthy Homes. It was then identified that there was a large risk to how she was getting in and out of her house. It was also identified that by not being able to easily leave her house, it was reducing her quality of life. Healthy Homes brought in a contractor to help build a wheelchair ramp for Ms. C. After the ramp was built, Healthy Homes went back to see how the ramp was working out for her. And with tears in her eyes, she said, 'I feel free!'. title: Andrea finds job, housing, education
what_changed: Andrea found a full-time job, stabilized her housing, and continued her education through an alternative school.
span_text: Andrea* is 17 years old.  She had to choose between a violent home or running away and taking her chances on the streets.  Fortunately, she had friends who let her sleep on the couch but without money and worse, no hope, she dropped out of school.  She had no future. Just by chance, Andrea met a Neighborhood House youth worker who encouraged her to set goals and helped her find solutions to all of her challenges.  Working together, Andrea was able to find a full time job, stabilize her housing and continue her education through an alternative school. Instead of worrying about her future, Andrea has set her eyes on her future.  She is committed to graduating from high school and pursue a career in the medical field.

title: John avoids electricity reconnection fees
what_changed: John avoided additional fees and got a boost to support his family.
span_text: John is a single dad with a chronic health condition. He is able to work part-time when his symptoms are under control, and otherwise he serves as the primary caregiver for his young children. As John's health has slowly deteriorated, he was able to apply for disability relief and he is currently waiting for a disability claim to be approved. Without this financial bridge, John is unable to pay his household bills. He contacted LISTEN this summer, fearful of not being able to afford his mounting electricity bills and the expensive fees to reconnect his service. Fortunately, we were able to step in to help him avoid any additional fees and give him the boost he needed to support his family.

title: Desiree's transformation at Rising Oaks

title: John's regained purpose and family
what_changed: John became a better husband, father, son, and brother, found purpose, and gained a new support network of brothers.
span_text: Heroes and Horses is a life changing program. When I retired in 2015 I felt lost and lonely, civilians just didn't understand who I was or what I had been through. Stepping out of my comfort zone with these horses and working with guys that 'had my back' helped me feel a part of something again, I had a mission and I had purpose. title: Addyson's third transplant succeeds

span_text: Ashley (pseudonym) was determined to make a better life for herself. Prior to her involvement with the Colorado Coalition for the Homeless (CCH), she worked many different jobs but felt drawn to truck driving. After being furloughed from her job in March of 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, she became involved with CCH through a family connection. title: Floyd's caricatures bring joy to residents
what_changed: Residents receive warm, whimsical caricatures that bring smiles and spark conversations about life, youth, and memories.
span_text: In the Kendal at Longwood Culinary Department, Marc Hopewell brings his own creativity to the community-but he isn't the only artist in the family. On special days, Marc's father, Floyd Hopewell, joins him at work, bringing his sketchbook and decades of artistic experience. Floyd sits with residents, chats with them, listens to their stories, and draws their caricatures-warm, whimsical portraits that capture not only their faces but also their spirits. These gatherings have become cherished moments. Residents welcome Floyd as a peer who understands their references and shares their humor. In return, Floyd uses his imagination to help people see themselves with joy and lightness, often sparking conversations about life, youth, and memories. His drawings bring smiles and sometimes remind residents of how they saw themselves years ago.

title: Historical research deepens residents' belonging
primary_beneficiary: Cartmel residents (Mark Knight, John Milner, and neighbors)
what_changed: Residents grew more deeply rooted in the present and feel an even greater sense of belonging to the place they call home.
span_text: Though the two researchers readily admit their findings can never be guaranteed-because the historical record is a patchwork-they embraced the challenge with enthusiasm. Piecing together the unknown made the story even more compelling. It wasn't about perfection; it was about connection. And through this journey, something meaningful happened. As they uncovered the community's past, they and some of their neighbors at Cartmel found themselves growing more deeply rooted in its present. The history they traced was full of human resilience, mirrored in the spirit they see in Cartmel today. Their work has sparked conversations, inspired neighbors, and perhaps helped some of them feel an even greater sense of belonging to the place they call home.

HIPPY es un programa basado en evidencia que: Mejora la preparación escolar Empodera a los padres como los primeros y más importantes maestros de sus hijos Aumenta el éxito académico a largo plazo El programa fortalece las interacciones entre padres e hijos mediante un aprendizaje estructurado basado en el hogar. span_text: This year, long-time Lebanon leader Terry Grigsby was honored with the Volunteer Service Award at the 2019 Spirit of NH awards. A volunteer at LISTEN's thrift stores for over 10 years, Terry has gifted the Upper Valley with several thousand hours of her time organizing jewelry and clothing to be sold in support of LISTEN's programs. A retired teacher, Terry has focused the next chapter of her life on helping our community in other ways. 'When I worked in  several of Lebanon's schools, I saw many families in need of the basics. I still know many people that must decide between purchasing food or heat. It is a good feeling to help in this way.'
